questions.question: "What are the classic mucocutaneous triad manifestations characteristic of dyskeratosis congenita?"

"In evaluating a late‑20s woman presenting with pancytopenia, ineffective erythropoiesis features on peripheral smear, very low reticulocyte count despite severe vitamin B12 deficiency, which inherited bone‑marrow‑failure syndromes would you consider alongside common acquired causes?"
"Explain how heterozygous missense mutations in the PARN gene may result in shortened telomeres and predispose to pulmonary fibrosis."

"Outline the diagnostic steps taken in this case—laboratory workup, imaging studies, upper gastrointestinal endoscopy—and explain how each helped rule out common acquired causes before considering a genetic telomere biology disorder."
"Describe the first‑line treatment strategy for severe vitamin B12 deficiency complicated by ineffective erythropoiesis characterized by basophilic stippling and Cabot rings."

"Why do patients with monoallelic pathogenic variants in PARN more commonly present with isolated idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis compared to patients with biallelic variants who usually have dyskeratosis congenita?"

"Name at least five non‑genetic causes that must be excluded when evaluating hepatic steatosis and cirrhosis in a young adult before diagnosing hepatic involvement secondary to a telomere biology disorder."
"Under what circumstances is hematopoietic stem cell transplantation indicated for patients with telomerase‑related bone‑marrow failure syndrome?"
